text:
sasha: Nightly eval spike on hi-IN numerals/ordinals prompt set. BLEU drop from 0.87 -> 0.62 on int8-nightly model. samples look like numerals/ordinals kept in latin or mangled. :eyes:

li-wei: Can you paste the eval summary + a few bad gens?

sasha: Sure. Eval run id: run-20260305-45 (eval-bot posted). Metrics:
```
macro_bleu: 0.62 (prev: 0.87)
accuracy: 0.71 -> 0.48
sample_count: 1200
subset: hi-IN-ordinals-numerals (w/ roman numerals + date formats)
```

sasha: Sample prompt 1 (EN->HI): "She finished 3rd in the marathon on 02/11/2024."
Baseline (release-202602): "उसने मैराथन में तीसरा स्थान हासिल किया 02/11/2024।"
New (int8-nightly): "उसने मैराथन में 3रा स्थान ले लिया 02-11-2024।"

marco: That's bad — ordinal marker collapsed to '3रा' and date delimiter changed. tokenizer mapping issue?

alex: Any code/ops changes yesterday? I saw a fused-kernel rollout for dot-product int8 on staging.

sasha: Yeah we rolled quant-gemm v2 (commit e4b9f3) to nightly around 01:10 UTC. eval-bot log: "quant kernel: gemm_fused_v2 enabled"

li-wei: Can we repro with CPU and float32 to check if it's quant-only?

sasha: Re-ran CPU/FP32 on same prompt: FP32 -> baseline correct. So quant seems implicated.

marco: Could also be tokenizer detokenization: ordinal suffix 'rd' attaches to token with punctuation handling. Quant affects softmax temp? but unlikely. We should run token-level alignments.

alex: Assigning bisect: sasha -> run nightly with previous kernel (gemm_fused_v1) and then with v2 but old tokenizer pipeline to narrow down.

sasha: On it. Also adding a small probe: run prompt set where ordinals are spelled out ("third") vs numeric ("3rd") to see sensitivity.

eval-bot: new run queued: eval://run-1767894321/compare-gemm-v1-v2

li-wei: If it's tokenizer mapping, check tokenizer.vocab entries for '3', 'rd', '3rd', and unicode normalizer changes.

marco: FYI, I saw a very small change in pre-tokenization PR that normalizes ordinals (PR #1024) — rolled to staging last week but not to main. Could be unrelated but mention.

alex: Good catch. Also check locale-aware postprocessing in generation de-tokenizer: hi-IN uses no space before punctuation. Might be interplay.

sasha: Plan: 1) repro with v1/v2 kernels, 2) run token alignment diff tool (token diffs + logits), 3) bisect quant code path if kernel implicated. I'll post updates here.

li-wei: Thx. If this is quant only, temporary mitigation: force FP32 fallback for hi-IN routes until fix.

sasha: Agreed. Will open infra ticket for safe-fallback: #infra-quant-fallback

marco: +1. Please also add failing examples to regression-triage board.

sasha: added 10 failing prompts to triage board: https://trello.internal/r/hi-in-ordinal-regress

eval-bot: run started: eval://run-1767894321/compare-gemm-v1-v2 at 1767894789

alex: Ping here when v1 reproduces baseline.

sasha: will update in ~30m, thanks.
